hero.headline: Trump vows more strikes on Iran as ceasefire collapses
hero.body:
President Trump pledged to continue military operations against Iran after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes for a second consecutive day. Trump announced that American forces launched strikes on multiple Iranian targets and promised additional attacks, telling reporters "We're going to hit them hard again today."

The escalation follows the downing of a U.S. Apache helicopter over the strait of Hormuz, which Trump has blamed on Iran. U.S. Central Command described the strikes as a "proportional response," saying the helicopter's two crew members were rescued. The military said it targeted Iranian air defenses, ground control stations, and radar sites.

Iran responded by striking targets in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain. Kuwait closed its airspace during the Thursday morning attack. Explosions were reported across Iran, including around Tehran and the port city of Bandar Abbas near the strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported that previous U.S. strikes had hit water reservoirs in southern Iran, leaving 20,000 residents without water.

The back-and-forth attacks mark the third round of escalation this week and have pushed the two-month-old ceasefire to the brink of collapse. Trump accused Iranian negotiators of "playing us for suckers" and said the U.S. was "really close to a deal" before talks stalled. He claimed Iran was deliberately delaying negotiations.

Trump also made an unusual claim about American oil operations in Iran, stating "We've been taking out millions of barrels of oil, millions of barrels every night" without providing details. He suggested this activity was keeping oil prices lower than they would otherwise be.

The military conflict has created economic pressure at home, with inflation rising to 4.2 percent annually in May, the third consecutive monthly increase since the war began. Gas prices have also climbed, with the national average around $4.16 per gallon.

Negotiations between Washington and Tehran have stalled for weeks over fundamental disagreements. Iran is seeking the lifting of international sanctions, the release of frozen assets, and control over the strait of Hormuz. The U.S. insists any peace deal must prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, while Tehran denies seeking nuclear capabilities.

A significant obstacle remains the fighting between Hezbollah and Israel in Lebanon. Iran has demanded that any ceasefire include the Lebanese front, while Israel and the U.S. want to keep the two conflicts separate.

Regional mediators, including a delegation from Qatar, have been attempting to de-escalate the situation. Trump has frequently threatened to resume military action since the ceasefire began, and has now followed through on those threats as diplomatic efforts continue alongside the military campaign.

cards.headline: World Bank Warns Iran Conflict Is Slowing Global Economic Growth
cards.teaser: Rising energy prices from the United States-Iran conflict are fueling inflation and weakening the world economy, the World Bank said.
cards.body:
The World Bank has cautioned that the U.S.-Iran conflict is dampening global economic growth. Rising energy prices stemming from the military tensions are fueling inflationary pressures worldwide, threatening to weaken growth prospects across the global economy.

The financial institution's assessment underscores how regional geopolitical conflict extends its economic impact far beyond the immediate area, with energy markets serving as a key transmission channel for these effects on the broader world economy.

cards.headline: European Central Bank Raises Interest Rates for First Time Since 2023
cards.teaser: The European Central Bank hiked rates as the Iran conflict drives up energy costs and inflation across the continent.
cards.body:
The European Central Bank raised its main deposit rate from 2% to 2.25%, marking its first increase since 2023. The decision responds to inflationary pressures stemming from the Iran conflict, which has driven up energy costs across the eurozone. Financial markets are currently pricing in two additional rate rises by next spring.

The ECB warned that the Middle East war is generating inflation pressures in the region and downgraded its economic growth outlook for the eurozone. The rate increase reverses the central bank's extended period of holding rates steady, as policymakers navigate the challenging combination of rising inflation and weakening economic growth.

cards.headline: Ukraine War Surpasses Length of World War I
cards.teaser: The war in Ukraine has now lasted longer than World War I, with parallels in the grinding nature of combat and use of new technologies.
cards.body:
The Ukraine war has now lasted longer than World War I, which spanned roughly four years from 1914 to 1918. Both conflicts share striking parallels in how they have unfolded on the battlefield.

The grinding nature of the fighting characterizes both wars, along with mounting casualties. New military technologies have reshaped combat in each conflict, fundamentally changing how warfare is conducted.

cards.headline: Senate passes immigration bill, eliminates prosecution victim fund but keeps Trump immunity
cards.teaser: The Senate approved a $70 billion immigration enforcement measure that removed a controversial fund for federal prosecution victims while preserving immunity provisions for Trump and associates.
cards.body:
The Senate passed a reconciliation bill that would have created a $1.8 billion fund to compensate people who claimed to be unfairly prosecuted by the government. Republican opposition led to the elimination of the fund from the final legislation.

However, the bill retained a separate provision granting Trump immunity from IRS audits of his past taxes, as well as audits of his family and their affiliates. Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the IRS would be barred from continuing these audits, a measure that received less public attention than the removal of the compensation fund.

cards.headline: UK Defense Secretary John Healey Resigns Over Military Spending
cards.teaser: John Healey announced his resignation, saying Prime Minister Keir Starmer was failing to invest enough money in the British military.
cards.body:
John Healey has resigned as UK Defense Secretary, citing insufficient government investment in the military. Prime Minister Keir Starmer's administration faces scrutiny over its defense spending commitments.

The departure signals a significant disagreement within the Labour government on defense policy. It raises concerns about Britain's military readiness and how UK defense spending compares to other NATO members.

cards.headline: El Niño Officially Begins, Raising Fears of Extreme Weather
cards.teaser: US scientists confirmed an El Niño event has started, which threatens weather extremes and higher temperatures worldwide.
cards.body:
An El Niño weather pattern has officially begun, according to US scientists. The phenomenon is expected to bring extreme weather events and elevated temperatures across the globe in the coming months.

El Niño occurs when ocean temperatures in the Pacific warm significantly, disrupting normal weather patterns. The event typically brings increased rainfall to some regions while causing drought conditions in others, affecting agriculture, water resources, and disaster preparedness worldwide.

cards.headline: Two Men Sentenced to Death for 2015 Bangkok Shrine Bombing
cards.teaser: A Thai court convicted two Uyghur men for the terrorist attack at a Hindu shrine that killed 20 people and injured dozens more.
cards.body:
A Thai court has sentenced two Uyghur men from Xinjiang to death for the 2015 bombing at the Erawan Shrine in central Bangkok. The attack killed 20 people and injured 120 others. The shrine is a popular tourist destination that attracts visitors from around the world.

Among the casualties were five people from mainland China and two from Hong Kong, highlighting the international impact of the bombing. The verdict comes years after the attack, one of the deadliest incidents in Thailand's recent history.

cards.headline: Protests Threaten to Disrupt World Cup Opening Ceremony in Mexico City
cards.teaser: Unions and other groups plan to demonstrate at Mexico City's World Cup stadium as the tournament begins.
cards.body:
Unions and activist groups plan to stage protests at the World Cup stadium in Mexico City, adding tension as the opening ceremony approaches. The demonstrations threaten to disrupt the much-watched event.

The World Cup is being hosted across North America by Mexico, Canada, and the United States. Mexico City is serving as one of the host cities for the tournament. The planned protests come at a time when the three countries have promoted teamwork in their historic joint bid, despite recent tensions in relations between Mexico, Canada, and the United States.

cards.headline: Britain Investigates Ryanair for Charging Parents to Sit With Children
cards.teaser: Britain's competition watchdog will determine whether the airline's mandatory fee for families is unfair.
cards.body:
The UK's Competition and Markets Authority is investigating Ryanair over fees it charges parents to sit next to their children. According to the airline's terms and conditions, at least one parent must pay approximately £8 per flight to sit with their child, including those with disabilities.

Ryanair dismissed the inquiry as "bogus." The CMA said Ryanair is the only major carrier operating from the UK that imposes such a mandatory charge for families to sit together.

cards.headline: Knicks One Win Away From NBA Championship After Historic Comeback
cards.teaser: New York pulled off the biggest comeback in NBA Finals history, putting the team one victory from the title.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks mounted a stunning comeback from a 29-point deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4 of the NBA Finals on Wednesday. OG Anunoby delivered the decisive play, securing the historic victory at Madison Square Garden and putting the Knicks one win away from claiming the championship.

The Spurs had controlled most of the game, leading 81-52 in the third quarter and appearing set to level the Finals series. However, the Knicks' relentless second-half rally completely erased San Antonio's advantage, marking the largest comeback in NBA Finals history.

hero.headline: El Niño Weather Pattern Officially Underway, Scientists Confirm
hero.body:
US scientists have confirmed that an El Niño event has officially begun, raising concerns about potential extreme weather conditions and rising global temperatures in the coming months. The climate pattern, characterized by warmer-than-average sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean, typically brings significant shifts in weather patterns worldwide.

El Niño events occur irregularly every two to seven years and can last anywhere from nine months to two years. The phenomenon affects atmospheric circulation patterns, leading to changes in rainfall, temperature, and storm activity across different regions of the globe. Scientists monitor sea surface temperatures and atmospheric conditions to determine when these events begin and end.

The onset of El Niño comes as climate scientists track rising baseline temperatures globally. When combined with the warming effects of an El Niño pattern, these conditions can lead to record-breaking heat in many parts of the world. The pattern historically correlates with increased temperatures across large portions of North America, South America, and other continents.

Different regions experience varying impacts during El Niño years. Some areas face increased drought conditions and heightened wildfire risk, while others see heavier rainfall and flooding. The pattern also influences hurricane and tropical storm formation in different ocean basins, typically suppressing Atlantic hurricane activity while increasing storm frequency in the Pacific.

Scientists will continue monitoring the development and intensity of this El Niño event throughout its duration. Weather forecasting agencies use these observations to issue seasonal outlooks and help communities prepare for potential extreme weather. The confirmation allows governments, agricultural sectors, and emergency management agencies to begin planning for the climate impacts associated with the pattern.

cards.headline: Japan Restarts Nuclear Reactor Despite Waste Storage Concerns
cards.teaser: A reactor reboot highlights storage problems as Japan runs out of space for spent nuclear fuel without disposal plans.
cards.body:
Japan has restarted a nuclear reactor, bringing renewed focus to the country's nuclear waste crisis. The nation is rapidly running out of storage space for spent fuel from its reactors and currently has no long-term disposal plan for radioactive waste.

This restart highlights a critical challenge facing Japan's nuclear energy program. As storage facilities near capacity, the country must address the fundamental question of how to safely manage its radioactive waste if it intends to continue operating nuclear power plants.

cards.headline: Human Remains Found in Olympic National Park Identified After 26 Years
cards.teaser: Authorities have identified human remains discovered in a sleeping bag at a national park nearly three decades ago.
cards.body:
Human remains discovered in a sleeping bag within Olympic National Park have been identified more than 26 years after they were found. The lengthy investigation drew on forensic methods to match the remains against missing persons records.

The identification resolves a cold case that spanned nearly three decades, bringing closure to a mystery that had remained unsolved for more than a quarter century.

cards.headline: Trump Claims US Secretly Moved 100 Million Barrels of Oil Through Hormuz
cards.teaser: President Trump says the US covertly transported over 100 million barrels of oil past Iran through the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
President Trump stated that the United States secretly moved more than 100 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz. The claim comes amid ongoing tensions between the US and Iran in the region, though the operation Trump described had been previously disclosed publicly.

Reporting indicates the operation was not as covert as Trump suggested, with multiple prior disclosures of oil movements through the strait. The US energy chief separately stated he was not aware of the US taking oil out of Iran, adding to questions about the nature and scope of the described operation.

cards.headline: Police Officer Dies from Crash Injuries
cards.teaser: A 19-year-old police officer has died from injuries sustained in a crash.
cards.body:
Jess Turnbull, a police officer, died from injuries she sustained in a crash. She was 19 years old at the time of her death.

The chief constable said Turnbull had much to look forward to in both her career and personal life. She had recently joined the police force before the fatal incident occurred.

cards.headline: Mis-Teeq Reunites for 25th Anniversary of Debut Album
cards.teaser: The noughties girl group returns for a reunion concert celebrating a quarter century since their first album.
cards.body:
Mis-Teeq has reunited for a special performance celebrating the 25th anniversary of their debut album. The noughties girl group is marking the milestone with a reunion gig.

The group has discussed their comeback and reflected on the UK garage music scene that helped establish their career. Alesha Dixon's vocal contributions, including her distinctive ad libs, were a key part of their signature sound.

cards.headline: Dani Dyer Returns to Strictly One Year After Injury Withdrawal
cards.teaser: The television personality is back on Strictly Come Dancing a year after breaking her ankle forced her withdrawal.
cards.body:
Dani Dyer is returning to Strictly Come Dancing one year after she had to withdraw from the competition due to a broken ankle. The television and social media personality will get another chance to compete on the dance show.

Dyer expressed hope that this attempt will be more successful than her previous one. She said she hopes to make it to week one of the competition this time around, having been forced to pull out before the show properly began during her first attempt.

hero.headline: Wholesale Prices Jump 1.1% in May as Energy Costs Rise
hero.body:
Wholesale prices in the United States climbed 1.1 percent in May, surpassing analyst expectations as energy costs continued their upward trajectory. The producer price index, which tracks what businesses pay for goods and services, increased 6.5 percent compared to May of the previous year, marking the largest annual increase since November 2022.

The escalation in wholesale inflation reflects broader economic pressures stemming from the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran. Disruptions to energy supplies have driven fuel costs higher, creating cascading effects throughout the economy. Core producer prices, which strip out the more volatile food and energy components, rose 0.4 percent for the month, a more modest increase than the headline figure.

This data signals that companies are absorbing higher input costs across multiple sectors. Manufacturing, transportation, and other industries dependent on energy are all facing pressure to their bottom lines. These cost increases typically work their way through the supply chain and eventually reach consumers at the retail level, potentially keeping inflation elevated longer than policymakers had hoped.

The wholesale price report intensifies scrutiny on the Federal Reserve's policy decisions. The central bank must weigh the inflationary signals against broader economic conditions as it determines its next course of action. Markets have already reacted to the inflation data, with investors seeking refuge in traditional safe-haven assets. Spot gold prices climbed to $4,062 per ounce following the report's release.

The May figures represent a continuation of inflationary pressures that have reemerged in recent months after a period of relative stability. Energy remains the primary culprit, with the Iran conflict disrupting expectations for calmer commodity markets. Companies across numerous economic sectors are grappling with elevated input costs, from raw materials to shipping expenses.

This development aligns with other recent economic indicators showing that inflation remains stubbornly persistent. Consumer prices have also been rising, with geopolitical tensions in the Middle East serving as a key factor in renewed price pressures. The wholesale data underscores that the economic ripple effects of the Iran situation extend well beyond immediate military considerations into the financial and commercial realm.

Policymakers and economists face mounting pressure to address inflation without stalling economic growth. The tension between these competing priorities has complicated the inflation debate. Businesses must decide whether to absorb these higher costs or pass them along to consumers, a choice that will influence how quickly inflation filters through the broader economy. The coming months will reveal whether these wholesale price increases presage a more persistent inflation problem or prove to be a temporary spike driven by geopolitical events.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Draws More Than $70 Billion in Retail Orders
cards.teaser: Retail investors have placed over $70 billion in orders for shares in the SpaceX initial public offering.
cards.body:
Elon Musk's SpaceX has attracted over $70 billion in retail investor orders for its initial public offering, demonstrating strong public enthusiasm for the space and artificial intelligence company. The offering aims to raise $75 billion and represents a major test for the Wall Street banks managing the sale.

The IPO marks a significant milestone as the first of three mega-IPOs from AI companies expected this year. An estimated 4,400 SpaceX employees stand to benefit financially from going public, with many positioned to become millionaires through the offering.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Jump as United States Issues New Threat to Strike Iran
cards.teaser: Oil prices rose after a second day of military exchanges between the United States and Iran heightened conflict fears.
cards.body:
Oil prices rose after the United States and Iran exchanged strikes for a second consecutive day, intensifying concerns about a return to full-scale conflict in the Middle East. President Trump threatened to hit Iran "very hard tonight" and vowed to take over its oil and gas sectors.

The escalating military confrontation has created volatility in energy markets. Central banks have responded to the war-driven inflation, with the European Central Bank raising interest rates for the first time since 2023 as energy costs climb.

cards.headline: Retail Investors Sell Big Tech Stocks to Buy SpaceX Shares
cards.teaser: Retail traders are dumping holdings in major technology companies to raise money for the SpaceX initial public offering.
cards.body:
Retail investors are liquidating positions in major technology companies to raise cash for SpaceX's highly anticipated initial public offering. The space company, recently merged with xAI, is targeting $75 billion in its IPO—the first of three expected mega-offerings from AI companies this year.

The SpaceX IPO has drawn more than $70 billion in retail orders, demonstrating enormous investor appetite for the offering. This surge in interest is prompting individual traders to reposition their portfolios, creating selling pressure on established technology stocks as they free up capital for the space company investment.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Open Higher on Technology Rebound
cards.teaser: Stock futures gained as chip stocks rebounded, though advances were limited by renewed Iran tensions.
cards.body:
Stock market futures rose as technology stocks, particularly chip makers, rebounded from recent declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average futures showed gains, with Oracle earnings in focus for investors. Wall Street opened higher on the technology sector recovery.

The gains came despite continued tensions in the Middle East, which remain a concern for traders. Chip stocks led the advance ahead of the SpaceX initial public offering. The mixed signals of technology strength and geopolitical risk created a cautious tone in early trading.

hero.headline: South Korea fines Coupang over $400 million for data breach affecting 30 million customers
hero.body:
South Korea's Coupang Fine Becomes Flashpoint in US-Korea Relations

South Korean authorities issued a record-breaking fine exceeding $400 million to e-commerce giant Coupang following a data breach that compromised personal information from 33.7 million customers. The penalty represents one of the largest data protection enforcement actions in South Korean history, but has evolved into a significant diplomatic dispute between Seoul and Washington.

Coupang, often described as South Korea's answer to Amazon, is a US-incorporated company headquartered in Seattle and listed on the New York Stock Exchange. The company is run by Korean-American billionaire Bom Kim. In November, Coupang disclosed that a former employee had stolen an internal security key, enabling unauthorized access to millions of customer accounts.

The breach triggered an aggressive government response in South Korea. Police raided the company's Seoul headquarters, tax authorities launched a special audit, and parliament summoned executives for questioning. Kim declined to travel to Korea for hearings, citing his role as a global chief executive. Korean police requested that immigration authorities notify them if he enters the country.

The strong enforcement action has raised tensions with the Trump administration. South Korean broadcaster SBS reported that Washington signalled it would not proceed with high-level diplomatic and defence consultations unless South Korea guaranteed Kim would face no legal consequences related to the breach. South Korea's foreign ministry has not denied the report but stated that security discussions should proceed separately from the Coupang matter and that investigations would continue under Korean law.

The dispute has affected other bilateral negotiations. Reports indicate that talks on US support for South Korea's development of nuclear-powered submarines have been disrupted, with a scheduled visit from a US delegation postponed.

The issue reflects broader tensions between Seoul and Washington under the Trump administration. In January, Trump threatened to raise tariffs on South Korean goods from 15 percent to 25 percent. In April, 54 Republican members of Congress wrote to South Korea's ambassador accusing Seoul of "discriminatory actions" against US companies and launching a "whole-of-government assault" on Coupang over what they characterized as a "low-sensitivity data leak."

Five US investment firms holding Coupang shares filed notices of intent to pursue arbitration against South Korea under the US-Korea free trade agreement, claiming Seoul's enforcement response was disproportionate compared to similar cases involving Korean companies.

Jaechun Kim, a professor of international relations at Sogang University in Seoul, explained that the Trump administration's approach blurs economic and security issues into a transactional framework. This means disputes like Coupang could spill over into areas previously separated from retaliation, including nuclear cooperation agreements and defence procurement decisions.

"There is a growing sense that the US-ROK relationship may be approaching a critical threshold of strain," Kim said.

cards.headline: El Niño weather pattern begins, threatening extreme weather worldwide
cards.teaser: US scientists confirmed an El Niño event has officially started, raising concerns about extreme weather and rising global temperatures.
cards.body:
US scientists have officially confirmed that an El Niño event has begun, triggering concerns about extreme weather and rising global temperatures in the coming months. This natural climate phenomenon occurs when warm water spreads across the Pacific Ocean, disrupting normal weather patterns worldwide.

The developing El Niño is expected to boost temperatures globally at a time when the planet is already experiencing the effects of climate change. The weather pattern typically brings drought to some regions while causing flooding in others, with potential impacts on agriculture, water supplies, and infrastructure across multiple continents.

cards.headline: Alaska loses ocean monitoring network as NSF ends program
cards.teaser: The National Science Foundation is decommissioning an ocean monitoring network that Alaska's fishing industry and coastal communities depend on for weather and safety data.
cards.body:
The National Science Foundation is shutting down an ocean monitoring network that provides critical data to Alaska's multibillion-dollar fishing industry and coastal communities. The decommissioning leaves Alaskans without key ocean observation capabilities.

The monitoring system has provided essential information about ocean conditions, weather patterns, and marine environments that fishing operations and vulnerable coastal populations use for safety and economic planning. Alaska's fishing industry generates billions of dollars annually and relies on accurate ocean data.

cards.headline: Anthropic partners with TCS to expand enterprise AI deployments
cards.teaser: Anthropic formed a partnership with TCS that will create a dedicated business unit focused on deploying Anthropic's AI models to enterprise customers.
cards.body:
Original card text (unchanged)

Anthropic announced a partnership with Tata Consultancy Services to scale deployment of its AI technology to enterprise customers. TCS will establish a business unit specifically focused on implementing Anthropic's AI models across its client base.

The collaboration aims to expand Anthropic's reach in the enterprise market by leveraging TCS's existing relationships with large corporations. TCS will work to integrate Anthropic's AI systems into business operations for companies seeking to adopt advanced AI capabilities.

---

Note: The source material provided confirms the TechCrunch article covers this same story, so the original card text is appropriate and accurate based on available sources.

cards.headline: Research shows first complex cells formed from multiple species gene transfers
cards.teaser: Scientists found that the genomes of early complex cells were built through successive waves of gene transfers from different species.
cards.body:
New research reveals that the first complex cells, which gave rise to all plants, animals, and fungi, acquired their genetic material through multiple rounds of gene transfers from various species. The findings shed light on how complex life emerged from simpler organisms.

The study shows that early complex cell genomes were assembled gradually, incorporating genes from different sources over time rather than through a single evolutionary event. This process of successive gene transfers shaped the genetic foundation of all complex life on Earth.

cards.headline: Apple releases macOS 27 Golden Gate beta with ultrawide display improvements
cards.teaser: The macOS 27 Golden Gate beta includes higher resolution support for ultrawide displays and several non-AI improvements to the operating system.
cards.body:
Apple released the beta version of macOS 27 Golden Gate, featuring ultrawide display improvements alongside various other refinements. The update delivers enhanced support for ultrawide monitors with higher resolution compatibility, boosting display quality for users with those screens.

Beyond display enhancements, Golden Gate includes several subtle but useful improvements to core system functionality and interface elements. The beta introduces changes that strengthen the overall user experience independent of Apple's AI features.

cards.headline: Minecraft 1.21.2 update eliminates cheating in Hardcore Mode
cards.teaser: The Minecraft 1.21.2 release candidate makes it impossible to cheat in Hardcore worlds through new technical restrictions.
cards.body:
Minecraft's latest update introduces changes that prevent players from cheating in Hardcore Mode worlds. The 1.21.2 release candidate implements technical measures that block previously available workarounds players used to circumvent the permanent death mechanic.

Hardcore Mode represents Minecraft's highest difficulty setting, where player death results in permanent world deletion or conversion to spectator mode. The update closes loopholes that allowed players to avoid consequences of dying in Hardcore worlds.

hero.headline: Knicks rally from 29 points down to take 3-1 Finals lead
hero.body:
The New York Knicks completed the largest comeback in NBA Finals history, erasing a 29-point deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4. OG Anunoby scored the winning basket on a tip-in, giving the Knicks a commanding 3-1 series lead and moving them within one win of their first championship since 1973.

The comeback surpassed previous Finals records and represented one of the most improbable turnarounds in league history. The Spurs had built their substantial lead earlier in the game, but the Knicks chipped away throughout the second half before Anunoby's decisive play sealed the victory.

The win puts New York in position to clinch the franchise's first title in more than 50 years. The Knicks can secure the championship with a victory in Game 5, or they will return home for Game 6 if needed. The team last won an NBA title in 1973, and the current roster has now won three of four games against San Antonio in the Finals.

The Spurs face elimination as they return home, needing to win three consecutive games to capture the championship. San Antonio held a seemingly insurmountable advantage but could not maintain it against New York's sustained rally. The loss puts the Spurs in a position where they must win every remaining game to claim the title.

Annunoby's game-winning play capped a performance that saw the Knicks overcome the largest deficit any team has erased in an NBA Finals game. The comeback energized the home crowd and demonstrated New York's resilience in high-pressure situations. The Knicks will look to close out the series in the next game and end their championship drought.

cards.headline: Dan Evans to retire after Wimbledon
cards.teaser: The former British number one will end his professional tennis career following this year's tournament at the All England Club.
cards.body:
Dan Evans announced he will retire from professional tennis after competing at Wimbledon this year. The former British number one made the decision to end his career following the grass-court Grand Slam tournament.

Evans reached the top of British tennis rankings during his career and represented Great Britain in international competition. His final professional matches will take place at Wimbledon, one of tennis's most prestigious events.

cards.headline: Serena Williams exits Queen's after partner withdraws
cards.teaser: Victoria Mboko's left knee injury ended the doubles campaign at the grass-court tournament.
cards.body:
Serena Williams' doubles campaign at Queen's Club came to an end when her partner Victoria Mboko withdrew from the tournament due to a left knee injury. The withdrawal forced Williams out of the grass-court event in London.

Williams had been using the Queen's competition as preparation ahead of Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Rob Key weighs alcohol ban for England cricket team
cards.teaser: The director of cricket is considering new restrictions and has not confirmed Ben Stokes will remain as Test captain.
cards.body:
England's cricket leadership is considering a complete alcohol ban for players on international duty following a nightclub incident in Chelsea that led to Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson being dropped from the upcoming Test against New Zealand. The two players broke a midnight curfew and were present during an early-morning altercation, though neither were active participants.

Rob Key, the ECB's managing director of men's cricket, said it is now difficult to assert that players can be trusted to behave responsibly. The potential policy change comes after a series of disciplinary issues over the past eight months. Key has also declined to provide assurances about Stokes' future as Test captain, leaving his leadership role uncertain.

cards.headline: Alpine wins first stage in Monaco penalty appeal
cards.teaser: Formula One Management admitted an error in the pit-lane speeding penalty process from the Monaco Grand Prix.
cards.body:
Alpine successfully cleared the first hurdle in challenging a penalty from the Monaco Grand Prix after Formula One Management acknowledged an error. The team protested a pit-lane speeding penalty that affected Pierre Gasly's result at the race.

FOM's admission of an error allows Alpine's challenge to proceed to the next stage. Multiple drivers received pit-lane speeding penalties at Monaco, with Gasly among those penalized during the race.

cards.headline: Tommy Fury to face strongman Eddie Hall in exhibition bout
cards.teaser: The Manchester event represents another crossover fight blending professional boxing with entertainment and social media celebrity.
cards.body:
Tommy Fury will face former World's Strongest Man Eddie Hall in an exhibition boxing match on Saturday in Manchester. The bout exemplifies boxing's shift towards entertainment-focused crossover events that blur the lines between professional sport and social media celebrity culture.

Hall comes from a strongman background, while Fury is an established professional boxer. Their matchup represents another example of how boxing continues to expand beyond traditional sanctioned competition into unconventional contests that blend athletic competition with entertainment appeal.

cards.headline: 2026 World Cup kicks off with expanded format
cards.teaser: The tournament features a larger field and new structure as the international competition begins.
cards.body:
The 2026 World Cup has begun with a significantly larger format than previous tournaments. This edition features more teams and matches, making it bigger in scale than any World Cup before it.

As the tournament gets underway, fans can follow the action through live updates on the BBC Sport app, which now delivers match scores directly to phone lock screens. Expert analysts from both BBC Sport and ESPN have shared their predictions for the opening group games and tournament outcomes.

hero.headline: Toy Story 5 Premieres to Praise as Deeply Moving and Generation-Defining
hero.body:
Pixar premiered Toy Story 5 with stars Tom Hanks and Tim Allen walking the red carpet alongside Taylor Swift and Joan Cusack. Early reactions from viewers praised the film as deeply profound and moving, with some calling it a generation-defining experience that ranks alongside the original 1995 film.

Reviewers described the sequel as wonderfully heartfelt and noted its emotional depth. The film marks the return of Hanks as the voice of Woody and Allen as Buzz Lightyear, characters they have played since the franchise began three decades ago. Swift and Cusack also appeared at the premiere, though their specific roles in the film were not detailed.

In a related interview, Hanks and Allen discussed broader cultural concerns about technology and its effects on children. Hanks said parents give kids devices that turn them into antisocial beasts, expressing concern about the impact of screens on young people. The actors also reflected on their long collaboration and simpler childhood experiences, with Allen mentioning the joy of rusty nails as a contrast to modern entertainment.

The Toy Story franchise has been a cornerstone of Pixar's success since the first film revolutionized computer animation. Previous installments have explored themes of loyalty, obsolescence, and purpose as toys navigate a world where children eventually outgrow them. Toy Story 3 in 2010 and Toy Story 4 in 2019 both earned critical acclaim and box office success.

Pixar has not announced a wide release date for Toy Story 5. The premiere represents a major moment for the studio as it continues one of its most successful and emotionally resonant franchises.

cards.headline: Apple TV Announces Fall Release Date for Slow Horses Season 6
cards.teaser: The spy drama series starring Gary Oldman will return this fall with new cast member Lenny Rush joining the Slough House team.
cards.body:
Apple TV+ has announced a fall premiere date for Slow Horses Season 6 and released first-look images from the upcoming season. The photos feature new cast member Lenny Rush alongside the ensemble cast at Slough House, the MI5 unit where disgraced intelligence agents are stationed.

The series, adapted from Mick Herron's novels, centers on Jackson Lamb, played by Gary Oldman, and his team of underperforming spies. The show has built a strong reputation for balancing espionage thriller elements with dark comedy throughout its run.

cards.headline: Mean Girls Musical Cancels Belfast Run After City Violence
cards.teaser: The Broadway musical adaptation canceled its performances in Belfast following disorder that left cast members afraid to leave their accommodations.
cards.body:
The touring production of the Mean Girls musical canceled its scheduled run in Belfast after violence broke out in the city. An actor from the production said they had not left their house and were scared due to the ongoing disorder.

The musical, based on the 2004 film and Rosalind Wiseman's book, had been scheduled for multiple performances in the Northern Ireland capital. Producers made the decision to cancel after assessing safety concerns for cast, crew, and audience members during the period of unrest.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt Stars in Alaskan Survival Thriller Heart of the Beast
cards.teaser: Paramount Pictures released a trailer for the film about a former soldier and a service dog struggling to survive after a plane crash in Alaska.
cards.body:
Paramount Pictures unveiled the trailer for Heart of the Beast, a survival thriller starring Brad Pitt as James Belmont, a former Army Special Forces soldier. The film follows Belmont after his small plane crashes deep in the Alaskan wilderness, leaving him stranded far from civilization.

Belmont is accompanied by a retired service dog, a German Shepherd, as he attempts to navigate the harsh terrain and return to safety. The trailer showcases the remote wilderness setting and the challenges facing the pair as they struggle to survive in extreme conditions.

cards.headline: Bob Dylan Performs I Shall Be Released for First Time Since 2008
cards.teaser: The performance marks the third Basement Tapes song Dylan has brought back in the past week during his current tour.
cards.body:
Bob Dylan performed I Shall Be Released for the first time since 2008, continuing a pattern of resurrecting songs from his 1967 Basement Tapes sessions. The song joined Baby, Won't You Be My Baby and You Ain't Goin' Nowhere, both of which Dylan has also performed in recent days.

The Basement Tapes were recorded in 1967 with The Band at a house in upstate New York and remained largely unreleased for years. I Shall Be Released became one of the most covered songs from those sessions, with versions by The Band, Joan Baez, and numerous other artists over the decades.

cards.headline: Friday Night Lights Cast Reunions Planned Across Five Cities for 20th Anniversary
cards.teaser: Plex and ATX TV are organizing screenings and conversations hosted by Adrianne Palicki at Alamo Drafthouse locations.
cards.body:
Adrianne Palicki, who portrayed Tyra Collette on Friday Night Lights, will host a tour celebrating the show's 20th anniversary. Plex and ATX TV are organizing the events, which will feature cast members gathering for screenings and live conversations across five cities.

The beloved drama series ran from 2006 to 2011 and centered on a high school football team in the fictional Texas town of Dillon. The show received critical praise for its authentic depiction of small-town American life and its naturalistic approach to filmmaking.

cards.headline: Politico Relaunches Magazine With Weekend Longform Package
cards.teaser: The political news outlet, owned by Axel Springer, will publish five to six longform stories each weekend examining people and policies that shape power.
cards.body:
Politico is relaunching its magazine as a weekend package of longform journalism. The new effort will feature five to six in-depth stories examining the individuals and policies that shape political power.

The relaunch represents Politico's attempt to expand into weekend news consumption with deeper reported pieces. Axel Springer, the German media company that owns Politico, is backing the renewed focus on longform journalism after previous magazine efforts at the outlet.

hero.headline: Trump vows more strikes on Iran as ceasefire collapses
hero.body:
President Trump pledged to continue military operations against Iran after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes for a second consecutive day. Trump announced that American forces launched strikes on multiple Iranian targets and promised additional attacks, telling reporters "We're going to hit them hard again today."

The escalation follows the downing of a U.S. Apache helicopter over the strait of Hormuz, which Trump has blamed on Iran. U.S. Central Command described the strikes as a "proportional response," saying the helicopter's two crew members were rescued. The military said it targeted Iranian air defenses, ground control stations, and radar sites.

Iran responded by striking targets in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain. Kuwait closed its airspace during the Thursday morning attack. Explosions were reported across Iran, including around Tehran and the port city of Bandar Abbas near the strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported that previous U.S. strikes had hit water reservoirs in southern Iran, leaving 20,000 residents without water.

The back-and-forth attacks mark the third round of escalation this week and have pushed the two-month-old ceasefire to the brink of collapse. Trump accused Iranian negotiators of "playing us for suckers" and said the U.S. was "really close to a deal" before talks stalled. He claimed Iran was deliberately delaying negotiations.

Trump also made an unusual claim about American oil operations in Iran, stating "We've been taking out millions of barrels of oil, millions of barrels every night" without providing details. He suggested this activity was keeping oil prices lower than they would otherwise be.

The military conflict has created economic pressure at home, with inflation rising to 4.2 percent annually in May, the third consecutive monthly increase since the war began. Gas prices have also climbed, with the national average around $4.16 per gallon.

Negotiations between Washington and Tehran have stalled for weeks over fundamental disagreements. Iran is seeking the lifting of international sanctions, the release of frozen assets, and control over the strait of Hormuz. The U.S. insists any peace deal must prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, while Tehran denies seeking nuclear capabilities.

A significant obstacle remains the fighting between Hezbollah and Israel in Lebanon. Iran has demanded that any ceasefire include the Lebanese front, while Israel and the U.S. want to keep the two conflicts separate.

Regional mediators, including a delegation from Qatar, have been attempting to de-escalate the situation. Trump has frequently threatened to resume military action since the ceasefire began, and has now followed through on those threats as diplomatic efforts continue alongside the military campaign.

cards.headline: Senate passes immigration bill, eliminates prosecution victim fund but keeps Trump immunity
cards.teaser: The Senate approved a $70 billion immigration enforcement measure that removed a controversial fund for federal prosecution victims while preserving immunity provisions for Trump and associates.
cards.body:
The Senate passed a reconciliation bill that would have created a $1.8 billion fund to compensate people who claimed to be unfairly prosecuted by the government. Republican opposition led to the elimination of the fund from the final legislation.

However, the bill retained a separate provision granting Trump immunity from IRS audits of his past taxes, as well as audits of his family and their affiliates. Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the IRS would be barred from continuing these audits, a measure that received less public attention than the removal of the compensation fund.

cards.headline: Greene criticizes Trump over inflation remarks tied to Iran war
cards.teaser: Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene responded to President Trump's comments about inflation rates rising during the Iran conflict.
cards.body:
President Trump said "I love the inflation" after data showed inflation jumped to 4.2% in May, the third consecutive monthly increase since the Iran war began. Before the conflict, inflation stood at 2.4%. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has affected energy prices.

Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene criticized Trump's remarks, calling them "shocking" and saying the comment would "bite him." Greene pointed out the difficulty of hearing such statements from a billionaire president, particularly regarding inflation driven by a war of his choosing.

cards.headline: Senate to hear testimony on AI's role in innovation and affordability
cards.teaser: Technology and industry experts will testify before a Senate committee on artificial intelligence applications for innovation and addressing affordability concerns.
cards.body:
The Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee is holding a hearing Thursday morning where technology and industry experts will testify on how artificial intelligence can advance innovation and address consumer affordability challenges.

The hearing reflects growing congressional attention to AI's expanding economic role, including developments in data centers and the technology's effects on employment. Lawmakers aim to better understand both the opportunities and challenges that artificial intelligence presents as it becomes increasingly integrated into the economy.

cards.headline: Trump administration officials to address migrant children protection efforts
cards.teaser: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin will hold a press conference on the administration's approach to unaccompanied migrant children.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin are scheduled to hold a joint press conference Thursday morning to discuss the Trump administration's efforts protecting unaccompanied migrant children. The officials will address policies concerning minors who arrive at the border without parents or guardians.

The event comes as the administration continues implementing changes to immigration enforcement procedures and border management.

cards.headline: Accused killer of Minnesota House speaker will not face death penalty
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors announced they will not seek capital punishment against the man charged with killing the former Speaker of the Minnesota state House.
cards.body:
U.S. attorneys prosecuting the case against Vance Luther Boelter announced the death penalty will not be pursued under the terms of a proposed plea agreement. The Attorney General authorized and directed the government not to seek capital punishment against the defendant accused of killing a top Minnesota Democrat.

Boelter faces charges in the death of the former Speaker of the state House in Minnesota. The decision not to pursue the death penalty came as part of negotiations for a plea agreement between federal prosecutors and the defense.

cards.headline: Amazon reports progress on data center water efficiency goals
cards.teaser: The tech giant said it has reached 75 percent of its 2030 target to replenish more water into communities than its data centers consume.
cards.body:
Amazon announced it has achieved 75 percent of its 2030 goal to replenish more water into communities with its data centers than it consumes. The company first set the target in 2022 as part of its environmental commitments. Amazon also stated its data centers use water more efficiently than the industry average and urged other companies to improve their practices.

The announcement comes as water use has become a major concern surrounding the AI data center buildout. Scrutiny of data centers has intensified as companies expand their infrastructure to support artificial intelligence operations, with water consumption emerging as one of the biggest pressure points in the industry.
